articles.title: Molten: Weld Pool
articles.summary: Dark glossy brown-orange with fine repeating crescent ripples, like frozen weld beads across the panel. Reads as a glowing orange-brown car with fine horizontal banding; the beads blur to a copper-brown shimmer with horizontal rhythm.
articles.what: The frozen ripple record of a moving arc, each crescent one pulse of the weld. Up close: Perfectly regular brick-offset rows of glowing orange oval beads, about 14 px wide, on a dark brown ground, each bead brighter in its middle with a slightly dark lower rim. Looks like stacked weld beads or a fish-scale pattern, tightly packed and aligned. From a distance: Reads as a glowing orange-brown car with fine horizontal banding; the beads blur to a copper-brown shimmer with horizontal rhythm. Measured spec (average): metal 229, roughness 35, coat 40. Shine: high gloss. Metal: full. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, stock car, truck / off-road.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Molten: Weld Pool" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and sides: long even rows read across broad panels
Small trim: fine enough to work
White or black numbers on a plate read; thin numbers shimmer with the bead rows.
Plain black or white stripes and number plates: bold shapes over the fine rows
Pairs well with: black, chrome, dark bronze, deep red.
pitfalls: Not crescent ripples: the render is round-ended ovals in offset rows, not curved arcs
Not smooth hammered copper: beads are distinct and aligned
Avoid: small text over the ripples, next to other metallic patterns.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 229 (true metallic), roughness 35 (high gloss), clearcoat 40 (strong-to-medium clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small text over the ripples, next to other metallic patterns.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: plain black or white stripes and number plates: bold shapes over the fine rows; large soft gradients: depth without fighting the beads
Patterns to avoid: other scale, weave, brick or carbon patterns: moire against the bead rows; fine glitter: noise
Spec overlays that work: gloss clear stripe zones: smooth patches for contrast; none needed: spec already carries the beads
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Flame: Wrinkled Front
articles.summary: Mid orange-tan mottled surface like coarse sand or sponge, satin, evenly rough all over with no pattern direction. Reads as a bright amber-orange with a coarse, gritty, wormy grain; dark gaps give it depth but it stays one warm colour.
articles.what: Michelson-Sivashinsky cusping: a flame front unstable to its own curvature, creasing everywhere. Up close: Tangle of short curly orange squiggles, like noodles or brain coral, 5-10 px thick, with dark brown shadow gaps between them. No direction, no cells; the orange is a bright amber with a few dark clumps. From a distance: Reads as a bright amber-orange with a coarse, gritty, wormy grain; dark gaps give it depth but it stays one warm colour. Measured spec (average): metal 105, roughness 60, coat 89. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: dirt late model, truck / off-road, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Flame: Wrinkled Front" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, and sides: broad panels show the squiggle
Bumpers also fine since the pattern has no direction
Black numbers with a white outline read; plain orange or tan numbers vanish.
Bold black or white stripes and graphics: orange ground is loud but even
Pairs well with: brown, cream, matte black, olive.
pitfalls: Not coarse sand: the render is curly worm-like squiggles, not round grains
Not a sibling recolour of Buoyant Fingers: same orange, but wormy and less veined
Avoid: mottle hides fine decals, low contrast for numbers.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 105 (pearl-level metal), roughness 60 (satin gloss), clearcoat 89 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: mottle hides fine decals, low contrast for numbers.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: bold black or white stripes and graphics: orange ground is loud but even; fine pinstripes along edges: easy to see
Patterns to avoid: other flame or crackle patterns: nearly the same family, no gain; grain, noise or dots: muddy
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat sweep: for a wetter look; none for metal: already medium
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
